description: Several keywords report against a containing object while the thing at fault is one member of it. Ajv carries that member's identity in err.params (missingProperty, additionalProperty, unevaluatedProperty, allowedValues, limit) and the wrapper prints only err.message, discarding it — which is why two extra members produce two identical lines. python-jsonschema puts the specifics in its message prose instead, so the two legs differ in how much they say rather than in what they found.

cases.name: two extra members produce one line each from ajv-validate, naming neither
cases.description: Two extra members, two failures, one containing object. The offending names are what distinguishes the lines.

defect.summary: ajv-validate emits one failure per offending member while jsonschema-validate aggregates them into a single message, so the legs report different numbers of lines.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: Additional properties are not allowed ('draft', 'note' were unexpected)
ajv-validate: INVALID: must NOT have additional properties
INVALID: must NOT have additional properties

cases.name: two unevaluated members produce one line each from ajv-validate, naming neither
cases.description: The same shape as the additionalProperties case, one keyword over.

defect.summary: ajv-validate emits one failure per offending member while jsonschema-validate aggregates them into a single message, so the legs report different numbers of lines.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: Unevaluated properties are not allowed ('draft', 'note' were unexpected)
ajv-validate: INVALID: must NOT have unevaluated properties
INVALID: must NOT have unevaluated properties

cases.name: two absent required members produce one failure each
cases.description: Two required members absent. Ajv names each in params; the Python leg names each in its message.

cases.name: an enum failure names the allowed values only on the Python leg
cases.description: Ajv's enum message names no values; the allowed set is in params.allowedValues. The Python leg quotes both the value and the set.

defect.summary: ajv-validate's line says only that the value must be one of the allowed values, because params.allowedValues is discarded.

ajv-validate: INVALID: must be equal to one of the allowed values

cases.name: a maxLength failure names the limit on both legs
cases.description: Ajv keeps the limit in params and happens to interpolate it into its message; the Python leg states it in prose.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: 'far too long' is too long
ajv-validate: INVALID: must NOT have more than 5 characters

cases.name: a type failure names the expected type
cases.description: Ajv keeps the expected type in params.type.

cases.name: each name propertyNames rejects is reported at its member, with no value found
cases.description: Both libraries locate a failing name at the object holding it, so without relocation every rejected name is the same finding. The site ends in the name; the member's value was not checked, so nothing is reported as found.

ajv-validate: INVALID: /inner: must be equal to one of the allowed values
INVALID: /inner: property name must be valid
INVALID: /inner: must be equal to one of the allowed values
INVALID: /inner: property name must be valid

defect.summary: ajv-validate prints an applicator's sub-results as peers of its conclusion; jsonschema-validate prints the conclusion alone, so the two legs report different numbers of lines.

cases.name: propertyNames false rejects each name at its member

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: /inner: False schema does not allow 'a'
INVALID: /inner: False schema does not allow 'b'
ajv-validate: INVALID: /inner: property name must be valid
INVALID: /inner: property name must be valid
